lesson_title: The Other Side of the Counter: Buying on Trust
hook_text: Somewhere in your supplier's office is a page with YOUR name on it. Here's how to owe money like a pro.
clip_script: Rule one: never pay an invoice on its own say-so. Before Metro's invoice earns a cent, three papers must tell one story: the order — what Thabo asked for; the delivery note — what the driver actually offloaded, counted and signed for at the door; and the invoice — what Metro says he owes. Three papers, one story: pay. Any mismatch — invoiced for ten boxes, received nine — is a debit note conversation, not a payment. This one habit stops a business paying for goods it never got, which happens to careless businesses more often than anyone admits.
visual_style: Three documents sliding together like puzzle pieces over a delivery doorway; a mismatch flashes red as one box goes missing from a stack of ten.
pacing: Firm rule-setting rhythm, tension on the mismatch, clean resolution.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — the creditors system, mirrored and mastered.
